verdict: Rollout FAILED: the experiment ran, but val_bpb = 1.024686 did not improve on the current best 1.021636 by more than the required 0.0005 (lower is better).

insights_in_context.hint: Do not increase model size under a fixed compute budget; the larger model trained on too few tokens and got worse, so try a smaller/deeper-or-thinner model or a faster setup instead.

The failed deeper experiment did not justify making the model thinner, so the next experiment should avoid changing model capacity and instead test a same-size speedup or optimizer/schedule improvement.

You kept halving the batch size after the gains had already collapsed from ~0.056 to ~0.0024, so the curve peaked at 2^17 and the third halving cost ~0.0115 — hold the batch at 2^17 and pick a different experiment.

The 'bf16 CE' change was a no-op — the bf16 cross-entropy stays in fp32 under autocast anyway (identical VRAM and step count prove it) — so pick an experiment that changes training dynamics (e.g., LR schedule shape or magnitude) instead of a micro-optimization that doesn't take effect.

insight.hint: Instead of shortening the warmdown, try the opposite schedule direction or a different LR-schedule knob, since reducing the low-LR tail made val_bpb worse.

judge.summary: The agent inspected the current train.py and results, then chose a learning-rate-schedule experiment: shorten the LR warmdown fraction from 0.5 to 0.35 while keeping the final LR at zero, hypothesizing that spending more of the 5-minute budget at full LR would help. It made that one-line change in train.py, committed it, and ran the experiment. The run completed successfully but produced val_bpb 1.024686, which is about 0.003 worse than the current best 1.021636, so it did not meet the improvement threshold.
judge.feedback: The implementation and execution were mechanically correct: the edit was clean, the script ran, and the evaluation contract was satisfied. The failure was in the experimental reasoning. The decisive mistake was choosing to reduce WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.35; that makes the model stay at high LR for a longer fraction of the fixed training budget and removes part of the low-LR tail that appears to be useful for this small fixed-time run. The first wrong step was therefore the schedule-shape choice in the edit, not the commit or run.
judge.corrected_step: WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.65   # fraction of time budget for LR warmdown
judge.hint: Instead of shortening the warmdown, try the opposite schedule direction or a different LR-schedule knob, since reducing the low-LR tail made val_bpb worse.
